cross_paper_synthesis.consensus: All provided answers confirm that the study (PMC4976365) reports specific parameters (strain rate 10^10 s^-1, temperatures 77-1000 K, strain cap 0.9%) and boundary conditions (NPT for lateral pressure) without explicitly linking these choices to specific failure outcomes like vacancy nucleation or validating the potential against bond-breaking energetics.
cross_paper_synthesis.different_approaches: The answers approach the methodology from distinct angles: one identifies a missing algorithm name for loading [a3c66b3a3afcd24a], another critiques the lack of validation for high-strain bond-breaking scenarios despite low cohesive energy deviation [d19ee3a3e9e80180], a third notes the gap in predicting defect nucleation [95b5ec547eb9c061], and a fourth highlights the ambiguity of the strain cap [ddaadbff2cfb9c7d]. A fifth answer uniquely interprets the physical consequence of the NPT boundary control [0927ada5aed3029f].
cross_paper_synthesis.condition_dependencies: The validity of the model for bond breaking is condition-dependent on whether the <2% cohesive energy deviation (observed at equilibrium or low strain) extrapolates to the high-strain regime where thermo-plastic instability occurs. Similarly, the accuracy of void nucleation predictions is dependent on whether negligible density change implies a lack of defect formation, a link not explicitly made in the text.
cross_paper_synthesis.contradictions: There are no direct contradictions between the answers. However, there is an implicit tension: the study claims to simulate high-strain deformation [d19ee3a3e9e80180], yet the engineering strain is capped at 0.9% [ddaadbff2cfb9c7d], which the answers collectively suggest may be insufficient to observe failure or saturation, creating a regime gap rather than a logical contradiction.
cross_paper_synthesis.evidence_strength: The evidence for specific algorithmic implementation is weak (algorithm named N/A) [a3c66b3a3afcd24a]. Evidence for the physical implications of boundary conditions is moderate (NPT allows lateral relaxation) [0927ada5aed3029f]. Evidence for model validity regarding bond breaking is explicitly absent or negative (no link established) [d19ee3a3e9e80180].
cross_paper_synthesis.unresolved_gap: It is unresolved why the engineering strain was capped at 0.9% and whether this limit prevents the observation of failure or saturation. Additionally, it is unclear if the negligible density change observed actually impacts the accuracy of predicting vacancy formation or void nucleation.
cross_paper_synthesis.candidate_hypothesis: The combination of the 0.9% strain cap and the NPT boundary condition (allowing lateral stress to relax to zero) prevents the simulation from reaching a state where true failure, saturation, or significant void nucleation can be observed or accurately characterized, effectively studying only the elastic/early plastic regime rather than the full failure process.
cross_paper_synthesis.discriminating_experiment: Run a separate simulation with fixed lateral boundaries (constant strain or traction control) to a higher engineering strain (>0.9%) and monitor the triaxial stress state and void nucleation events directly, comparing these results against the NPT zero-pressure lateral boundary case to quantify the deviation from a true triaxial failure state.
